title: Where in Paul's Life Was Each Letter Written?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Drag the seven undisputed letters of Paul onto a timeline of his life, using one clue from inside each letter.

learningObjectives: Organize the seven undisputed letters onto a timeline of Paul's life, using one clue from inside each letter, placing all seven in an accepted period within two attempts.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Evidence-based ordering: drag cards onto a timeline using internal clues, with two checks and reasoned feedback
keyQuestions: Where was Paul, and who was with him, when he wrote each letter?
Why do most of the letters fall in the third journey?
Why is the place of the prison letters still debated?
commonMisconceptions: Paul's letters were written in the order they appear in the New Testament, so Romans came first.
All the prison letters were written in Rome at the end of his life.
Paul wrote letters throughout his thirty years of travel; the seven come from about ten years, most from the third journey.
assessmentOpportunities: All seven letters placed in accepted periods within two Checks.
Explain why 1 Corinthians can be placed in Ephesus with certainty but Philippians cannot.
